text:
**LiFePO4 is the better choice for most buyers.** Almost every current power station uses it, and the main advantages of NMC are narrow.

**Why LiFePO4 wins**

- **Cycle life:** The sources rate LiFePO4 units at roughly 3,000 to 6,000 cycles to 80% capacity. NMC is rated lower, though the sources disagree on how much lower. [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/) lists NMC at 500 cycles, while [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc) gives 1,000 to 2,000. For daily use, that gap decides the question. Note that cycle ratings also depend on the end-of-life capacity target (70% vs 80%), so compare the full claim.
- **Safety:** In the lab studies cited by [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), LFP cells peaked at about 259 °C during thermal runaway, while NMC cells reached about 731 °C. LFP failures were milder, though not fireproof. This matters most for indoor or in-vehicle use.
- **Cost:** [PowerStationMatch](https://powerstationmatch.com/learn/lifepo4-vs-nmc) and [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) report that the price gap has largely closed. Their median prices were about $0.55 per Wh for LiFePO4 and $0.95 per Wh for NMC. LiFePO4 is usually cheaper per cycle.

**Where NMC has an edge**

- **Weight:** NMC stores more energy per pound, but the advantage is smaller in finished products than in cells. [OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/) found a median of 39.2 Wh/lb for NMC against 35.5 Wh/lb for LFP. Some LFP units are lighter than NMC ones, so compare specific models.
- **Availability:** NMC now appears mostly in older or compact models. [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc) counted 3 NMC units among 128 listed.

**Which to pick**

| Your use | Pick |
|---|---|
| Daily or near-daily cycling (van, off-grid, solar) | LiFePO4 |
| Indoor or vehicle storage, safety-conscious | LiFePO4 |
| Weekend use where weight matters most | Either; compare models |
| A few outages a year | Either; store per the manual |

Chemistry matters less than fit. Size the station to your loads first, then pick the chemistry. Also check the manufacturer's charging temperature range, since the sources note that it depends on the product as well as the chemistry.

**Example LiFePO4 unit:** The [BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-elite-200-v2) is a 2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4 station rated at 6,000+ cycles to 80%, with a 2,600 W inverter, a 24.2 kg weight, and a 5-year warranty. The listing I found showed $899 as of October 24, 2026. The link is an affiliate link, and the site says it earns a commission on purchases, so prices may have changed. Check the store's checkout for the current price.
